channel.title: Notes by Brian Busch
channel.description: Notes on cartography, spatial analysis, and GIS applications by Brian Busch, GISP.

item.title: Traffic Flow on Salt Lake County's State Highways
item.description: A print map of 2025 annual average daily traffic on the state highways of Salt Lake County, Utah. Line width shows the traffic on each count section.

item.title: Reading First Light Off a DEM
item.description: A DEM-based method in ArcGIS Pro for predicting when the sun clears a desert rim, checked against a known landmark before trusting the result.

item.title: UGEM Hub
item.description: How the UGEM Hub, the emergency management GIS site for Utah, went from placeholder cards to working guides and checked links in fall 2026.

item.title: One place to see the water in the West
item.description: How a job-interview map became the Western Water Dashboard: reservoirs, snow, and drought for eleven western states, rebuilt with AI agents.

item.title: No test goes red on a misleading name
item.description: AI agents wrote most of the Western Water Dashboard under written rules. The failures that mattered were about meaning, and the tests stayed green.

item.title: Millcreek Planning Map
item.description: Millcreek's public planning and zoning map, rebuilt on the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript with Nearmap aerial imagery, shareable links, and a text alternative.

item.title: Millcreek Property Lookup
item.description: A text-only property report for Millcreek, Utah. Type an address to get zoning, flood hazard, district, and utility facts without a map or a mouse.

item.title: Turning sidewalk gaps into a connected trail network
item.description: How Millcreek turned scattered sidewalk and trail studies into one citywide map a department director can act on, with sidewalk data from aerial imagery.

item.title: Turning a General Plan into a public map
item.description: Millcreek planners lost meeting time to a six-page General Plan appendix. This work made it one 4 ft by 6 ft wall map of all 13 future land use categories.

item.title: Millcreek Redistricting
item.description: How Millcreek combined ArcGIS Pro analysis and a public StoryMap/Survey123 feedback loop to redraw its City Council districts after the 2020 Census.

item.title: WUI Boundary Mapping
item.description: Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) boundary mapping for Utah local governments, covering HB 48 and HB 41 compliance workflows.

item.title: Alcohol Spacing Regulations
item.description: A map and interactive web app visualizing alcohol-establishment spacing regulations across Millcreek, Utah.

item.title: Keeping neighboring polygons apart
item.description: A Python (ArcPy) script that gives a different color to each adjacent polygon.

item.title: One drought dashboard, two WebGL renderers
item.description: A Utah reservoir drought dashboard built on the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JS, then rebuilt in MapLibre GL JS as an open-source parity comparison.

item.title: Western Reservoir Storage
item.description: Monthly storage at 405 western reservoirs, replayed over the Western Water Dashboard’s ArcGIS basemap.

item.title: Two Lakes, Two River Systems
item.description: Lake Mead and Lake Powell as daily elevation lines, then the Colorado and Columbia reservoir systems drawn as diagrams.

item.title: Drought in 75 Western Basins
item.description: The U.S. Drought Monitor map for October 27, 2026 across 75 western basins, then ten years of each basin's share of land in severe drought or worse.

item.title: Utah Wildfire Starts by Cause
item.description: 37,882 Utah wildfire records with known causes, 1992–2024. Maps compare natural and human-caused starts as points and density surfaces.

item.title: What the Canyon Overlook Trail Sees
item.description: A modeled walk along Zion’s Canyon Overlook Trail. Nearly half the visible ground first appears in the final 15 m. Bare earth, with no trees or buildings.

item.title: Holmes's 1882 Zion Panorama, Redrawn
item.description: A new drawing of W. H. Holmes's 1882 Zion panorama, using USGS elevation data and an estimated viewpoint.

item.title: A 10-Minute Walk to Transit on the Wasatch Front
item.description: Using 2020 Census counts and UTA’s published schedule, this model estimates walking access to transit in four Wasatch Front counties.

item.title: Great Salt Lake at 4,198 Feet
item.description: Great Salt Lake at 4,198 feet, the low end of the Strike Team's healthy range: about 474 square miles more lake than on November 3, a 51% gain.

item.title: Nine in Ten Utahns Live on About 1% of the Land
item.description: In the 2020 Census, 89.8% of Utahns lived in 25 urban areas on 1.1% of the land. The rest of Utah held 10.2% of residents on 98.9% of the land.

item.title: One Prompt, Six Maps of Japan
item.description: One shared prompt, six earthquake maps, and a 30-minute limit for each. What six models produced from the same brief, and what one review found.

item.title: One Prompt, Seven More Maps of Japan
item.description: The Day 10 brief, run by seven more models from four companies. Times, tokens, list-price costs, all seven posters, and what the checks found.

item.title: The Mighty Five, by Decibel
item.description: The NPS sound model compares existing and natural sound across Utah. Five park meters show the share at 6 dB or more.

item.title: A Field Guide to the Megawatt
item.description: 48 Utah solar farms, each scaled to one megawatt at one ground scale. The median footprint is 5.9 acres of panels per MW AC.

item.title: Drive Times to Utah's Five National Parks
item.description: Drive times from every place in Utah to its five national parks. Within 4 h 30 min of driving, 63% of Utahns can reach all five.

item.title: The Zion Narrows in Lidar
item.description: The Narrows of Zion National Park, drawn from USGS lidar points in Blender. A slot canyon that you walk in the river, as a Borgesian labyrinth.

item.title: Who Measures the West's Reservoirs?
item.description: Nine public sources report the storage of 424 reservoirs in 11 western states. Select a source to light its reservoirs on a 3D map.

item.title: 2 Years of Utah in 136 Photographs
item.description: A Reel of 136 edited Dust & Starlight photographs landing on a map of Utah in the order of their capture dates. The Reel shows 24 in full.

item.title: Sun and Shade on the Walk to the Subway
item.description: A terrain model of direct sun in the Left Fork of North Creek, Zion National Park, with a GPS track from a hike to the Subway on November 12, 2026.

item.title: The Reservoirs the Dashboard Does Not Show
item.description: 151 of 497 reservoirs of 10,000 acre-feet or more in five western water regions are not on the Western Water Dashboard. A map sorts them by kind of absence.

item.title: Scent Strata
item.description: Twelve plant communities of Utah's five national parks on one elevation scale, each with its published smell, under a 3D block of the Grand Staircase colored by plant community.

item.title: Forty Years of Ground
item.description: Utah's land cover in 1,023 hexagons, 10 miles across, each raised to its mean elevation, with close-ups of six hexagons from 1985 to 2025.

item.title: Utah Ski Runs, Rated and Measured
item.description: One plate for each of 14 Utah ski resorts, from OpenStreetMap's runs and lifts, with each run measured at its steepest 330 feet on USGS elevation.

item.title: 79 Ways to Flatten Utah
item.description: Utah's draft State Plane Coordinate System of 2022 has 79 low-distortion zones, each with its own projection. Two posters map the zones and show how long a mapped mile is against the ground.

item.title: Utah's Fruit Belts
item.description: Utah's two fruit belts and the historic orchards of Fruita in Capitol Reef, mapped field by field on aerial imagery from the state's 2025 water-related land use data.

item.title: Where a Raindrop in Utah Ends Up
item.description: Every stream in Utah, colored by where its water ends up by the drainage network, with line width by mean annual flow, from the NHDPlus Version 2 stream data.

item.title: The Subway as a Gaussian Splat
item.description: Eighty seconds of GoPro video from the Subway in Zion National Park, rebuilt as a gaussian splat, mapped from a bird's-eye view, and open to explore in 3D.

item.title: Four Rivers in Relative Elevation
item.description: Four western rivers show how low ground and old channels emerge when height is measured from the river surface.

item.title: Shading the San Rafael Swell
item.description: Eight tests with Eduard Cloud show how nearby terrain changes the shaded relief of the San Rafael Swell.

item.title: Exposure Around Moab
item.description: Five cliff edges near Moab show how far the ground drops within 164 feet of where a person can stand.

item.title: The Last Two Days: Six Palettes and Five Drawn Maps of Utah
item.description: The last two days of the challenge. Day 29: one shaded relief of Utah in six color ramps. Day 30: one brief, one fixed map of Utah’s five national parks, and five AI models that each drew and signed it.

item.title: Utah Dark-Sky Points
item.description: Utah's International Dark-Sky Parks mapped as points, for the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Utah Scenic Byways
item.description: All 27 of Utah's Scenic Byways, 1,893.84 miles of roadway symbolized as line features, for the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Utah Government Land Ownership
item.description: Government land ownership across Utah, federal agencies and state trust lands, styled in Esri's Firefly look, for the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Utah Population Hexagons
item.description: Utah Population Density: A Hexagonal Perspective. A 30 Day Map Challenge map that sums Census 2020 population into a 50-square-mile hexagon grid.

item.title: Old Spanish Trail
item.description: The Utah segment of the Old Spanish National Historic Trail, mapped for the A Journey theme of the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Shading terrain the Imhof way
item.description: An Imhof-inspired hillshade of Utah's terrain, built for the Raster theme of the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge using Esri's Terrain Service.

item.title: Vintage Atlas Style
item.description: Utah's urban areas and rivers in a vintage cartographic style inspired by the 1854 David Rumsey Map Collection, for the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Utah Localities via HDX
item.description: Utah's populated places mapped from a single humanitarian dataset, for the Humanitarian Data Exchange theme of the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: AI-Generated Fictional Map
item.description: A ChatGPT-generated fictional map of Utah water resources, for the AI theme of the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge. Kept for what it gets wrong.

item.title: Utah Counties, Pen & Paper
item.description: Utah's counties and county seats in a hand-drawn pen-and-paper style, for the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Avalanche Paths
item.description: A 3D map of avalanche paths in Little Cottonwood Canyon, styled for an Arctic aesthetic, for the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.

item.title: Utah Time and Space
item.description: Mule deer migration pathways across Utah's Paunsaugunt Plateau, mapped for the Time and Space theme of the 2024 30 Day Map Challenge.
